title: An early Public Interest Litigation
body: A lawyer, Mrs. Kapila Hingorani, read in a newspaper that many under-trial prisoners in Bihar were still in jail even though their trials had not finished. Some of them had already spent more time in jail than the punishment they would have received if they had been found guilty. She was not one of the prisoners, and she was not related to them. Still, she filed a writ petition before the Supreme Court asking for the release of all such under-trial prisoners. The Supreme Court immediately ordered their release and also issued guidelines that led to the release of almost 40,000 under-trial prisoners across India. This is described as the first reported case of a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India.

title: A flat that was never built
body: In 2011, a builder announced a plan to construct a complex of flats. A family decided to buy one of the flats and paid an advance of almost Rs 65 lakh. Over the next four years the family visited the site regularly, but there was no sign of any building where their flat was supposed to stand. The family felt that the builder had broken the agreement. They filed a complaint before a specialised forum that decides such disputes. After listening to both sides, the forum ordered the builder to return the money with interest and also to pay the family's cost of the litigation.
